decisions.reason: As a stated flagship closely aligned with the firm's reusable-packaging strategy, it retains high option value and is unlikely to be withdrawn absent clear failure signals.
A multi-model foldable large container line with its own page in both observed years fits the core business well, so management would likely keep this scalable option open.

Although it had lower web prominence, a stackable plastic crate is a core, low-carry-cost extension of the existing packaging portfolio and is worth retaining while demand potential continues to resolve.
The rackable pallet line is adjacent to established pallet capabilities and showed no clear early failure, so a large firm would typically keep it on the market and monitor performance.

Its drop from a dedicated page to a mention suggests weaker traction in a narrower niche, but as a related pallet line with limited incremental carrying cost it is still slightly more likely to be kept for another year.
This pallet variant looks more specialized and less central than the flagship launches, yet it remains close to the firm's core offering and thus still has enough residual option value to keep.
